q: I’m a bit “crunchy,” and being a first time mom, I stocked up on books, did a ton of research about different birth outcomes, and generally just did my best to prepare for the birth.
cx: Twelve weeks postpartum, a first-time mother on how she prepared before a birth that went differently.

q: In a way, I think that being so “flexible” and “mentally prepared” for “any” outcome was my way of feeling like I had some degree of control over things. Deep down, I thought that because I had done so much to prepare & had done my research…that things would go exactly how I wanted them to.
cx: What she now thinks her preparation was really for.

q: One of the books I read […] The information she shared in there - beyond even c-sections, made me feel…afraid.
cx: A pregnancy book she read left her more afraid.

q: For the following 2-3 weeks, I was pretty mopey about the birth. I had a hard time grasping how I could be so incredibly happy about our sweet boy, but simultaneously mourn the birth I spent so much time secretly hoping for.
cx: Her feelings in the first weeks after the birth.
r: unit: emergency surgical birth; postpartum emotions

q: I feel like it’s good to share these things - the good, the bad, the ugly. Not to scare people, but to highlight to mama’s that truly, sometimes no matter how much you prep, something unexpected can happen.
cx: Why she shared a realistic birth story.

q: I’m happy that even tho this isn’t what I expected for my pregnancy, I can still enjoy it just as much.
cx: At nine weeks, after a hard stretch with housing and family, things are improving.

q: No one at my new job knows, but I’ve known most of these people for half a decade so I know that when I do tell them it will be exciting and happy.
cx: Not yet told her workplace at nine weeks.

q: Good luck to anybody doing it soon - its a pain like no other but it disappears in an instant and it is totally worth it in the end🫶🏼
cx: The day after a long UK induction, to women still waiting.

q: I suppose in the end I had my dream birth which was no hormones or c-section (although I was begging for a c-section whilst his head was half out🤣)
cx: After pain relief failed, she gave birth with gas and air.

q: Now off to navigate breastfeeding……
cx: What comes next the day after the birth.

q: Naturally—being the anxious person I am—I spent the entire weekend doom-scrolling and reading every article, thread, and study I could find.
cx: An Italian husband waiting on further tests after a first-trimester screening result.

q: In Italy, it costs anywhere from €400 to €2,000, but it is worth every single cent for the peace of mind
cx: What the couple paid out of pocket for a prenatal test after a scare.

q: I was a birth story junkie during this pregnancy and I think it helped me getting in the mindset that if unmedicated birth was possible for others, it was possible for me too.
cx: Second birth (she has a toddler); what she says got her mind ready.

q: In my mind she was going to be my savior with the low intervention pain management plans we had discussed (tens unit, birthing comb etc). She is nowhere to be found.
cx: Her doula missed the fast birth, waiting in the car park.

q: DH firmly told me he was gonna go get the truck started and he was sorry if we did get turned away but that was his decision.
cx: Her husband overruled her wish to keep labouring at home.

q: I tell him “I don’t think I can do this anymore” and he is silent (good husband).
cx: The drive to hospital in late labour.

q: Loved laboring at home, being comfortable in my own bed, hot water from the shower.
cx: What she rated highly in her 9/10 birth.

q: I found it so helpful to read stories on this subreddit during my pregnancy, so wanted to contribute my own in the hopes that it's useful to someone.
cx: UK mother sharing her birth story after an unplanned route.

q: While it wasn't anything like what I had planned/hoped for (quite the opposite, actually) […] overall I feel like I had a good experience.
cx: Her verdict on a birth that went against her plan.

q: My husband is a great advocate and asks for a few minutes so we can discuss things privately.
cx: What her husband did at the decision point in labour.

q: I have a little cry as I'm a big mess of emotions - frustrated that I haven't gone into labour spontaneously, exhausted by the recent lack of sleep on top of the general pregnancy exhaustion
cx: How she felt after two days of a slow induction.

q: Our midwife managed to wangle a private room for us overnight so we could have a bit of privacy to decompress and regroup, which was really appreciated.
cx: What made her first night after the birth easier.

q: The best piece of advice I received about birth as someone who had sooo much anxiety about it was to only look at the positive stories, so I wanted to share mine!
cx: A few days after the birth, passing on advice she was given.

q: Coming from someone who’s been terrified all pregnancy to have this baby - don’t overwhelm yourself with horror stories!!
cx: Her message to pregnant readers.

q: I knew 100% going into this that I wanted the epidural and so I opted to get one at that point knowing I wouldn’t be able to handle them much longer.
cx: Deciding on pain relief before an induction.
